passage: Ines stood on a small stool at the low table in Lisbon, her tongue between her teeth. She had a damp cloth and a serious face. Esther, her mother, sat with her tea and did not move. Ines wiped in big circles, and water ran over the edge onto the floor. She missed the crumbs near the edge. "Done!" she said. Esther looked at the wet table and the drip on the floor. She said, "Thank you, Ines, that helps. Shall we do the corner together?" Ines beamed and pushed the cloth over the last crumbs. Then she stood back and said proudly, "I am a helper."

qa.q: What did Ines use to wipe the table?
How did Ines feel when she said "Done!"?
qa.a: Ines felt proud and important, even though the table was still wet and had crumbs.

qa.q: What did Esther do that made Ines want to keep helping?
qa.a: Esther thanked Ines, did not take the cloth away and offered to do the corner together.

qa.q: What might Esther be thinking as she looks at the wet table?
qa.a: Esther can see it is messy, but she is patient and values Ines feeling useful more than a perfect table.

grounding: Shows a young child proudly wiping a table slowly and messily, and a parent patiently accepting the imperfect help.

passage: At snack time, Irawati, the nursery teacher, handed out the paper plates. "Who wants to be plate helper today?" Vasudha's hand shot up. She carried one plate at a time from the pile to each friend, slowly, with both hands, her lips pressed together. The third plate slipped and clattered on the mat. Vasudha froze and looked up. Irawati smiled. "Plates fall. Pick it up and carry on." Vasudha picked it up. When all the plates were down, she stood at the front, chest out. "I did the plates," she said. Irawati gave her a small sticker of a star.

qa.q: Who was the plate helper at snack time?
qa.a: Vasudha was the plate helper at snack time.

qa.q: What was Vasudha feeling when the plate clattered on the mat?
qa.a: Vasudha was startled and worried about being in trouble, which is why she froze and looked up.

qa.q: What did Irawati do that helped Vasudha keep trying?
qa.a: Irawati smiled, said plates fall and asked Vasudha to pick it up and carry on.

qa.q: How might the other children feel as Vasudha hands out the plates?
qa.a: The other children probably feel pleased to be served by a friend, and may want a turn as plate helper.

grounding: Shows a young child carrying plates slowly and clumsily, with a teacher accepting imperfect help and building confidence.
